purpose: Independent review of donor-relative static hardware registration before marker calibration
scope: Pose-only OpenSim; temporary serialized model only; no integration, IK solve, policy or operational mutation
decision: Accept as explicit AB06-relative benchmark convention; does not measure AB07 acquisition floor or qualify gait

contract.independent_anchor: Every vertex of the fixed, unscaled AM_foot_l.STL attached directly to foot_l
targets: Median per-pose minimum STL clearance to shared binary-profile plane
Median static sagittal hardware inclination, atan2(n dot R eX, n dot R eY)
allowed_changes: Constant ankle-coordinate offset in static marker-calibration motion only
protected: Whole model XML except distal mount Y, including MarkerSet, SEA, axes, default angles, ranges, mass/COM/inertia
Frozen profiles, controller/config, dynamic healthy targets
requires_afterwards: Recalibrate markers against registered static motion
Qualify dynamic contact and event behaviour independently
reject: Absolute STL sole Y=0 imposed as if surveyed
Using binary virtual points or force-envelope spheres to fit anatomy
Changing detector reach, plane, thresholds, SEA or controller to obtain registration

limitations: Benchmark-relative registration, not a measured physical floor or shoe model.
STL visual geometry defines the common registration convention, not the online sphere contact law.
Ankle offset applies only to the static marker-calibration motion, not to runtime commands or joint zero.
New marker IK and contact/event qualification remain required; matching static geometry alone is insufficient.

independent_native_serialized_model.method: Separate STL struct reader; full independent coordinate setting and angular-unit conversion; native body stations define actual serialized foot transform

checks: Actual AB06 exact XML and motion identity
Newly loaded AB07 native geometry against donor medians
Monotone median crossing instead of median shortcut
Mixed/zero sensitivity, nonfinite inputs, collapse/inversion, invalid normal/mount, unchanged ankle bounds

limitations: STL is visual hardware geometry and selects a documented common convention, not an independent physical floor or shoe contact survey.
The donor itself has a calibrated virtual ground and contact profiles; target matching transfers that convention rather than asserting absolute physical correctness.
Median clearance and pitch do not require every sample or vertex to contact the ground.
Static matching cannot establish dynamic GRF, heel-strike coverage or event timing; the subsequent native IK and rollout must be reviewed separately.
